name: 4am IRR - for the inner IRR nerd in you!
page_title: RSVP to 4am IRR - for the inne… | Partiful
event_description:
Please, please, please.....Where are all of the Internal Rate of Return nerds?

This virtual session is for you!

Starting at 4am, that was not a typo (don't worry if that is too early, you can register for the replay).

Looking for like minded IRR enthusias that want to make history by attending the first event of New York Tech week. 

There's something special about being first that is oh so sweet. 

Running for only 30 minutes (so you can go back to sleep if needed) this session will cover 3 of the most important IRRs (there are over 15).

The IRRs covered are:
Modified IRR ✔️ 
Time Zero IRR ✔️ 
De-annualized IRR ✔️ 

Last year tech week I hosted the miseducation of IRR and that event was a blast so I'm looking to do things a little different and kick start tech week with the first event happening. 

For those of you not familiar with IRR, IRR or Internal Rate of Return is the famous (or infamous depending on who you talk to) calculation that is used to evaluate Venture Capital and Private Equity Returns.

Despite having it's weaknesses, the calculation is fraught with it's avid users in the Private Capital Markets. 

So grab your coffee, tea or matcha and attend the first event of New York tech week. 

Note a recap will be emailed to all those who cannot make it as some attendees are bound to oversleep given the time. 

The recap/replay will be available during the entire text week for you to enjoy.

This event is a part of #NYTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com

page_title: Japan Gateway for Climate & De… | Partiful
event_description:
Where will climate and deep tech actually scale—and with whom?
As AI-driven energy demand accelerates and geopolitical shifts reshape global supply chains, investor focus is moving toward one critical question: which markets, platforms, and partnerships can turn innovation into real-world deployment.
At the same time, cities and states across the U.S. are taking on a more decisive role in shaping the conditions for that deployment. Governors in 24 states—representing approximately 60% of the U.S. economy and 55% of its population—remain committed to climate action, while 46 states and more than 350 cities continue to advance local initiatives. Beyond federal policy, these subnational dynamics are becoming increasingly central.
In parallel, attention is turning to partners capable of supporting the transition from proof of concept to commercialization. Japan, with its deep industrial base, advanced manufacturing capabilities, and global corporate networks, is emerging as a critical partner in enabling large-scale deployment—particularly in sectors such as energy systems, infrastructure, and materials.
This event will convene investors from the U.S. and Japan, along with policymakers and industry leaders, to share insights on these trends from a U.S.–Japan investor perspective, and to explore where and how the next phase of scaling will take place through emerging opportunities for U.S.–Japan collaboration.

name: From Vibe Coding to AI-Driven Development
page_title: From Vibe Coding to AI-Driven … | Partiful
event_description:
AI is radically changing how software is built. Tools can now generate prototypes in hours — sometimes minutes. But speed alone doesn’t create successful products.

​​​This side event explores the real difference between “vibe coding” — fast, AI-generated code driven by intuition — and AI-driven development with an expert in the loop, where AI accelerates delivery without sacrificing quality, security, or long-term value.

We’ll break down when rapid AI prototyping is good enough, when it becomes risky, and how founders, product leaders, and innovation teams can use AI responsibly to deliver MVPs that are not just fast — but fundable, scalable, and production-ready.

​​​What you’ll learn?

​​​Vibe Coding vs AI-Driven Development
Understand where AI-only coding works, where it fails, and why expert oversight is the difference between a demo and a real product.

​​​The hidden risks of fast AI-built MVPs
Learn why many AI-generated prototypes collapse under investor scrutiny due to poor architecture, security gaps, and technical debt.

​​​Expert-in-the-loop MVP delivery
See how experienced engineers and architects guide AI to ensure clean architecture, compliance, scalability, and knowledge retention.

​​​From idea to production roadmap
Get a practical blueprint for turning AI-assisted prototypes into systems that can survive real users, real traffic, and real growth.

​​​Who should attend?

​​​First-time startup founders
Learn why flashy demos rarely convince investors — and how to build an MVP that balances speed with credibility.

​​​Serial entrepreneurs
Discover how to reduce MVP cost and timelines without repeating mistakes that lead to fragile systems and lost ROI.

​​​Enterprises & innovation teams
Validate new product ideas quickly while keeping core engineering teams focused — and avoid creating future technical debt.

​​​Product & tech leaders
Understand how to integrate AI into your development process without losing control over quality, security, or strategy.

​​​Why attend?

​​​AI won’t replace engineering expertise — but teams that combine AI with the right experts will outperform those who rely on speed alone.

​​​This session is a practical, no-hype conversation about how modern teams build software responsibly in the age of AI — whether you’re launching your first startup or innovating inside a large organization.

name: Design Thinking Meets AI: Book Talk & Live Build
page_title: Design Thinking Meets AI: Book… | Partiful
event_description:
AI can write the code now, but who's designing what it builds? Louise Macfadyen, author of the newly released O'Reilly book, Designing AI Interfaces, joins Bethany Crystal for a conversation that starts with a deceptively simple question: What does it mean to design AI-native systems and interfaces?

​Together they'll explore the philosophy and surprises of designing AI systems, poking at questions like: Who counts as a designer now? What does good taste looks like in a prompt-driven world? What happens when the coding is the easy part? Then they'll put it to the test.

Bethany and Louise will take a design concept from the book and build it live, in real time (using AI), showing what it looks like when design thinking drives the engineering, not the other way around. They'll close with a reflection on what worked, what surprised them, and what it means for anyone building with AI today.

​Key Takeaways:

- ​Understand the core principles of AI interface design from the author who literally wrote the book on it

- ​Watch design thinking applied live, from concept to working prototype in real time

​- Rethink your own role: You don't need to be a "designer" to start designing better AI experiences

​Target Audience:

- ​Product managers, designers, and builders working on AI-powered products who want a sharper design lens

- ​Founders and operators using AI tools daily who want to move from "it works" to "it works well" and understand why the difference matters

- ​Copies of the book, Designing AI Interfaces, will be available for purchase.

​—

​Co-hosts: Bethany Crystal (Founder & CEO, Build First - https://buildfirst.ai/) + Louise Macfadyen (Author, Designing AI Interfaces, O'Reilly Media)

Networking and drinks after. 

Lucy spent 10+ years in global HR, Culture & Capability for Fortune 500 companies, but started her career as a games designer. She now is a founder of a self service AI Adoption Platform, advises companies on AI workforce strategy and teaches AI to leaders at General Assembly. 

Andrea is a Partner at DHR Global (top 6 exec search firm), a Perplexity Fellow, and has 25+ years matching talent to value across life sciences, healthcare, and tech.

Max Horton is a Director at Oakleaf Partnership, leading the firm’s New York office, specializing in executive search across the CPG, manufacturing and life-sciences sectors. name: Healthcare AI In the Clinic - Panel & Networking
page_title: Healthcare AI In the Clinic - … | Partiful
event_description:
The conversation around AI in healthcare has gotten loud. Most of it skips the hard parts: regulatory exposure, integration complexity, and whether the investment actually shows up in the numbers.

Confido Health is bringing together investors, operators, legal experts, and healthcare leaders for an honest panel on what is actually changing across outpatient healthcare.

The discussion covers three areas that keep coming up in boardrooms and operating committees: how AI is reshaping M&A strategy and investment theses in outpatient providers, where regulation is heading and what that means for organizations deploying AI today, and what it takes operationally to move from pilot to production across multi-location groups.

Whether you run operations at a DSO or MSO, advise PE-backed healthcare platforms, or are evaluating AI for your own organization, this panel is designed to be useful, not theoretical.

Moderated by Dr. Raihan Faroqui, VP of Partnerships at Confido Health, the panel brings together voices that rarely share a stage.

Confido Health has deployed across more than 1,000 sites, and those deployments inform the conversation throughout. But this is not a product pitch. The goal is to give PE operating partners, AI and technology advisors, MSO and DSO leaders, and healthcare operators a room where the questions are practical and the answers are grounded in what these groups are seeing right now.

name: True Confessions:AI Hype & Fundraising
page_title: True Confessions:AI Hype & Fun… | Partiful
event_description:
What would you say about AI right now if no one could trace it back to you?

TRUE CONFESSIONS is a candid, facilitated conversation about the AI boom's real impact on fundraising. We'll cut through the hype so founders and investors can make better decisions based on what's actually happening.

Hosted by Flywheel Strategy x Tech/ish during NY Tech Week, this session brings together investors, AI founders, and non-AI founders for a structured discussion grounded in anonymous feedback and sentiment from those in the room and outside experts.

The Problem

AI hype is distorting capital markets — pressuring AI companies to overstate, making non-AI founders feel locked out, and skewing perception for everyone keeping up through headlines.

How It Works

Attendees complete an anonymous pre-event survey where unpopular opinions are welcome. We open by sharing what the room actually believes: where investors feel pressure to deploy, where AI founders feel pressure to overstate, where non-AI founders feel locked out. Then we dig in.
No panels. No pitching. No performative takes.

You'll Leave With

- Clarity on signal vs. hype: a grounded read on what’s actually driving AI fundraising decisions right now (and what’s just noise)
- Unfiltered market insight: real, anonymous sentiment from founders and investors you won’t hear on stage or in press cycles
- Actionable positioning edge: how to navigate (or leverage) the AI narrative whether you’re building in AI or not, to raise and compete more effectively

It feels distant — something for “later.”

But in reality, exit is not a final milestone. It’s a filter applied from day one.
Every early investor is implicitly asking:

*Can this company scale into something public markets will understand?
Will institutional capital show up at exit?
*Is the path structurally clean — or broken before it begins?
*That lens shapes which companies get funded, how they’re valued, and what paths remain open.

And here’s the part most founders don’t realize: NASDAQ’s Capital Market Equity Standard requires only a two-year operating history.Meaning many companies could be IPO-ready within ~36 months — if the right capital and structural decisions are made early.

This Panel Connects the Full Capital Lifecycle. Bringing together perspectives across every stage:

*A pre-IPO investor who writes the checks that signal IPO readiness
*A public-market investor who decides whether to buy on opening day
*A recently IPO’d operator who just navigated the transition

Together, they map the critical inflection points across the journey —
what to build, what to prove, and what fundamentally changes when the company becomes investable to institutional capital.

What Founders Will Learn
*How VCs actually think about exit potential at the earliest stage
*What makes a company investable across multiple rounds — not just one
*The structural decisions that expand (or limit) your future capital options
*Why most startups become uninvestable long before they realize it

About the Host — Allin AI
The only platform founders will ever need across their capital journey.
From startup to public company, we help companies: be seen → be investible → get funded → stay funded

Not a point solution — an operating system for capital formation across the entire lifecycle.

name: How to Write a Book on AI in Enterprise SDLC While Patterns Keep Changing
page_title: RSVP to How to Write a Book on… | Partiful
event_description:
New model drops. New framework. New "this changes everything" thread. By the time you've integrated one tool, three more have made it obsolete.

So we asked ourselves a different question: what doesn't change? Across enterprise teams, across codebases, across the hype cycles. Which engineering practices actually hold up when the underlying models rotate every quarter?

Artur Skowroński and Tomasz Lelek spent a year shipping AI-assisted code across enterprise clients, watching what broke and what survived, then committed the patterns to print in Vibe Engineering: Best practices, mistakes, and tradeoffs, co-published with Manning Publications.

Join Artur and Tomasz for a discussion panel and community mixer, and learn about:
- Where AI earns its place in the delivery cycle, and where it creates new debt 
- Vibe coding beyond the individual contributor: what changes at team and org scale
- Keeping quality and trust intact when half your code has a co-author 
- Staying fast without losing control of what ships

And if you are interested in writing a book yourself, Artur and Tomasz will also talk about:
- Picking the right topic, so that the trend is still relevant when the book is out
- Getting past the writer’s block
- What reputable publishers like Manning are actually looking for right now

After the panel, you are invited over for drinks, networking, and the kind of conversations that don't happen in Slack.

Bonus: We'll be giving away 30 demo copies of Vibe Engineering: Best practices, mistakes, and tradeoffs. Grab one and get it signed by Artur and Tomasz in person.

event_description:
You’re building with AI and moving fast. You may not have the budget for a full-time in-house lawyer or a big-firm billable rate, but you still need to make real decisions about data, governance, and corporate structure. In the age of AI, gaps in data governance aren’t just compliance issues anymore—they turn into technical debt that’s harder and more expensive to unwind later. When selling your AI-powered products, there are questions vendors must be prepared to answer and defend.

Join Yelena Ambartsumian (AIGP, CIPP/US), founder of AMBART LAW, and Princess Uchekwe, founder of The Chief Counsel, for a straightforward conversation about how to get real legal help without hiring a full-time GC. A fractional GC is an experienced lawyer who joins your team part-time and on a flexible scope, so you get ongoing, business-savvy legal support at a cost a startup can actually carry.

For decades, the systems that underpin work — benefits, healthcare, and financial stability — were built around a single assumption: one job, one employer, one steady income.

That assumption is breaking.

name: Innovate, protect, monetize: Navigating IP rights and infringement risks in the age of AI
page_title: Innovate, protect, monetize: N… | Partiful
event_description:
Join Norton Rose Fulbright during New York Tech Week for an intimate happy hour at the intersection of innovation, intellectual property and artificial intelligence.

As AI reshapes how companies create, compete and commercialize, a strong IP strategy is no longer just about protection. It's about turning your intellectual assets into meaningful revenue while navigating an increasingly complex legal landscape. This evening will explore how founders, technologists and legal leaders can move beyond defensive IP strategies to actively monetize innovation in the AI age, without stepping on the rights of others.

Partner Johanna Schmitt and Counsel Sam Eichner from Norton Rose Fulbright's Brands Group, along with Stephanie DeBrow from the firm's Patent Disputes practice, will kick off the evening with a brief presentation covering timely topics, including:

Monetizing your IP
• Copyright in the age of AI: Who owns AI-generated content? How are courts and regulators approaching authorship, fair use and training data liability?
• Trademark strategy for AI-driven brands: Protecting and monetizing brand identity in a world of AI-generated names, logos and marketing assets
• Patent monetization: Structuring licensing programs, identifying monetization opportunities and navigating patent disputes in emerging tech
• Building a holistic IP portfolio: Integrating patents, trademarks, copyrights and trade secrets into a coordinated commercial strategy
• Licensing and commercialization: How companies can structure IP licensing deals to generate revenue and strategic advantage in AI-driven markets

Avoiding infringement: What tech businesses need to know
• Copyright clearance & AI training data: Understanding the risks of using third-party content to train AI models and how to implement responsible data sourcing practices
• Trademark clearance and brand adoption: Why conducting thorough clearance searches before launching a new brand, product name or logo is essential, and what the consequences of skipping this step can be
• Patent freedom to operate: How to assess whether a new product or technology infringes existing patents before going to market, and strategies for mitigating exposure
• Open source compliance: The often overlooked IP obligations that come with incorporating open source software into commercial products
• Third-party content and licensing: Best practices for securing rights to images, music, text and software to avoid unintentional infringement across your platforms and products
• Employee and contractor IP assignments: Ensuring your business actually owns the IP created by those working for it, and avoiding disputes over ownership down the line

Following the presentation, join us for drinks, conversation and networking.

name: The Internet of Building Things
page_title: The Internet of Building Thing… | Partiful
event_description:
Since 1999, when MIT researcher Kevin Ashton coined the phrase "Internet of Things," the promise has been to track vehicles, equipment, and cargo in real time.

In 2026, that promise is finally becoming practical. A new logistics stack is emerging built on RFID, BLE beacons, cellular telematics, cameras, and satellite connectivity. Devices can now run 10 years on a battery with hourly pings, and new systems are even experimenting with Bluetooth signals detected directly by satellites.

The recent Vancouver HardTech Forum on 'The Internet of Moving Things' discussed how continuous monitoring throughout the supply chain is now the standard. For #NYTechWeek, we're turning to the job site with "The Internet of Building Things."

Construction has always been one of the hardest environments to digitize—chaotic, temporary, GPS-denied, and constantly changing—but autonomous drones are mapping progress in real time, LiDAR systems are generating centimeter-accurate 3D models without a surveyor on site, and the same sensor stacks that track fleet assets on highways are being adapted to track equipment, materials, and workers across active builds.

Zoom out and the same forces are reshaping the broader built environment — from utilities using robotics to manage infrastructure across thousands of miles, to smart buildings generating telemetry streams that rival industrial systems.

This HardTech Forum will ask: now that we can see the physical world with unprecedented resolution, where does the real value get created? In the hardware, the data, or the platforms that turn sensor feeds into decisions?

#A16Z #techweek #AI #Travel

Jetzy collaborates with A16Z techweek to invite you to The Future of AI — an exclusive event where you'll witness SAI, the world's most advanced AI assistant, perform real work on a real computer — right in front of you. Unlike chatbots that give you answers, SAI operates your computer—browsing the web, filling out forms, creating files, sending emails, and completing multi-step tasks from start to finish. It's like having a brilliant executive assistant who never sleeps and never forgets.

No slides. No buzzwords. Just AI doing actual work. 

🔍 Find You a Job: SAI searches openings, matches your skills, tailors your resume, and drafts applications — in minutes

💰 Raise Capital: SAI identifies the right investors, pulls their contact info, drafts personalized outreach emails, and builds your pipeline

📊 Prepare Any Report: Name a topic — market analysis, competitive research, financial modeling — SAI researches, writes, and delivers a polished document

And much more.....

_____________________________

Ang Li is the founder of Simular that owns SAI. 

Ang says:

What if your computer could work independently, just like a human assistant?

After a decade in AI research at Google DeepMind, something still deeply puzzled me: we spend 2.5 hours daily just moving our computer mouse. That's 30% of our work time on mechanical tasks.

This realization led me to build Simular AI. We're creating AI agents that use computers like humans do - clicking, typing, and navigating interfaces - so you can focus on what truly matters.

My journey spans:

- Research: 42 papers in top AI venues (NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, ICLR)
- Engineering: Scaled AI systems at Google (Ads, Maps, YouTube)
- Leadership: Built & led teams in autonomous driving
- Competition: 2x World Finalist in ACM/ICPC

Now, I'm on a mission to democratize AI assistance. Because the future of work isn't about replacing humans - it's about augmenting them.

Want to see the future of human-computer interaction?
→ Visit simular.ai
→ Follow my insights on X @angli_ai

page_title: Storytelling Dinner Series wit… | Partiful
event_description:
Think Moth Theater meets a Jeffersonian Dinner!

Every night we’ll gather a small group of fintech and DeFi founders and VCs around a table for a delicious meal and a single, shared conversation about the topic of the night.

It's an opportunity to meet each other without having to pitch or make small talk. See the real people behind the business.

The dinner series will take place over three nights in the middle of the NYCTechWeek. We will invite only 15 people each night. 

The themes are:
Tue, June 2 - "Risk"
Wed, June 3 - "Conviction"
Thurs, June 4 - "Incentive"

We picked the themes around finance, but they can be interpreted broadly. What was the riskiest thing you've ever done? What unexpected incentives are you creating with your kids? When was a particular conviction of yours tested? Share your nugget of experience with us.

​Bring one to three short stories connected to the theme of the night to share.

Why one to three? Think one to share, two in the pocket.
Usually, when you start thinking of one, a few more pop up and we don’t want them to go to waste:

​One to Share: Pick your favorite story. The one you’re most excited to tell. You'll share this one first.

​Two in the Pocket: Have two more ready just in case. If we move fast and there’s more time to share, we’ll invite popcorn-style sharing.

​There is no specific format or expectation in length (try to keep it under 5 minutes, be mindful of people’s attention spans). 

It can be a written-out essay, a poem, a toast, or a story that you improvise on the spot, or even someone else's writing as long as you give the author credit.

If you decide to improvise, maybe try to at least have an idea of which story you’re telling and have a couple of bullet points in mind. 

​The goal isn't a perfect performance; it's about sharing something real. Something that you feel deeply.

​The Flow of the night:

​6:30 PM: Arrive, grab a drink, and meet some fellow storytellers.

​7:30 PM: We’ll sit down for dinner and stories. (We take a small break in the middle.)

​9:00 PM: We wrap the stories up.

​9:30 PM: Good night!

name: LOCK UP AI?
all_hosts: Unmute; Healthcare Club of New York
page_title: LOCK UP AI? - #NYTechWeek | Partiful
event_description:
In partnership with the Healthcare Club of NY and Caseflow AI (usecaseflow.ai) for NY TECH WEEK.

New York is about to decide something the rest of the country will be watching: whether chatbot companies should be on the hook when their AI gives medical, legal, or mental health advice that causes harm.

Senate Bill S7263, sponsored by State Senator Kristen Gonzalez, would make chatbot operators civilly liable when their AI provides "substantive" advice in domains covered by professional licensing law. That's 14+ licensed professions plus the practice of law. Disclaimers don't save you. A "you're talking to a bot" notice doesn't save you. And the private right of action means anyone harmed can sue.

Supporters say it's common sense: if a human pretending to be a doctor can be prosecuted, a chatbot that hallucinates a medical license shouldn't get a free pass. Critics say the bill is vague about what counts as "substantive" advice, puts nonprofit and government chatbots in the same legal crosshairs as OpenAI, and ends up taxing the people who most need low-cost information (tenants, patients, small business owners) on behalf of licensed incumbents who don't love the competition.
Both sides have a point. That's why we're putting them in a room.

Against S7263:
Sateesh Nori: attorney, legal tech founder (LawDroid), and one of the more thoughtful voices arguing that restricting AI legal guidance hurts the people the legal system already fails.

For S7263:
Dr. Cecilia Dones: data and analytics practitioner-academic, founder of 3 Standard Deviations, and a faculty member at Columbia's School of Professional Studies. Her work sits at the intersection of AI, data, and trust: translating what these systems actually do for organizations, consumers, and the people who get caught in between.

UNMUTED: Where talking points go to die.

page_title: Build Your Team for the Agenti… | Partiful
event_description:
Build your team for the AI Era: A working session for founders and operators

Not a panel. Not a presentation. A hands-on session where you leave with something real.

Most teams are letting people go, handing work to agents, and then realizing no one knows how to manage, debug, or course-correct when things break. The org chart isn't just a people problem anymore and most teams have no framework for thinking about it.

What we'll do:

Part 1: Design Getting everyone on the same page, literally. We'll start with a shared vocabulary (what is an AI agent vs. AI, what is an AI Orchestrator, where do agents sit in a reporting structure) and then work through how to reimagine an org chart with both human and agent roles mapped explicitly. Where does discretion live? Where does transactional work get handed off? Who owns the system when it breaks?

Part 2: Implementation Once the design is clear, the harder question: how do you actually build toward it? This is where workflow architecture, change management, and the culture of how humans and agents operate together come into focus.

What you'll walk away with:

1) A reimagined version of your org structure and new roles identified, handoffs mapped. 
2) A "Before & After" org chart visualization showing where agents plug in and where humans move up to Orchestrator. 
3) An AI usage diagnostic: where you are vs. where you could be

***Bring your laptop to be able to participate in the session.

Why Britt & Mina: Britt has spent four years deploying fractional operators onto early and growth-stage teams, a model that's essentially a preview of where all teams are heading. Mina brings the AI implementation layer, including a sharp framework for thinking about agents the way we once thought about org hierarchy. page_title: The Age of Influence in B2B Ma… | Partiful
event_description:
Traditional marketing and communications are undergoing a seismic shift as the line between B2B and B2C strategies continues to blur. Modern B2B buyers no longer exist in a vacuum of dry sales data and technical white papers; they move fluidly between expert voices in media, social influence, independent analysts, and industry peer communities. • Social & Influencer Extensions: Leveraging executive visibility and online influencer advocacy networks to expand brand reputation beyond traditional earned media.
• The AI Gatekeeper: Understanding how AI search, GEO and LLMs increasingly act as the first interpreters of information, requiring content that is authoritative, structured, and "human-led" to be surfaced.
• Themed Content Ecosystems: Moving away from siloed content toward interconnected storytelling that addresses the "rest, motion, and work" lifestyles of C-suite decision-makers.

With marketing budgets reaching five-year lows and "shrinkflation" putting pressure on decision-makers to deliver more for less, the ability to build trust and authority as a B2B tech brand is paramount. This discussion will provide actionable insights into how to bridge the gap between high-level awareness and product-driven conversion by utilizing a mix of digital marketing, communications, and web content expertise.

event_description:
Future of Flight: From Innovation to Certification

The next generation of aerospace products will not be defined by technology alone. Bringing novel aircraft designs to market requires certification strategy, regulatory alignment, operational integration, infrastructure readiness, public trust, and the capital discipline needed to move from concept to certified product.

Hosted during NY Tech Week, this panel will explore what it takes for emerging aerospace manufacturers to bring certified aircraft to market and safely integrate advanced aircraft into the National Airspace System. event_description:
💡 What’s the Ugly Truth
People are not going to shop the way they do now forever. The shift is already starting. Consumers will increasingly ask AI agents to search, compare, recommend, and in some cases buy for them.
That means brands cannot rely on the old playbook alone. If discovery moves from browsers and marketplaces to AI-led interfaces, brands risk losing attention, pricing power, customer data, and margin.
The real question is not whether agentic commerce is coming. It is whether your brand will know how to compete when the buyer is no longer a person clicking through your storefront, but an AI making the shortlist.

🎯 Why You Should Attend
-Learn what agentic commerce actually looks like right now, not just the hype.
-Understand how shopping behavior may shift over the next 5 to 10 years.
-Get clear on what parts of the old ecommerce playbook still matter, and what is starting to break.
-Learn where brands should invest now to stay discoverable, defensible, and profitable.
-Avoid expensive mistakes around channels, data, pricing, and customer acquisition.
-Meet the founders, operators, and researchers shaping this shift in real time.

🙋 Who's Getting In This Room
-Brand owners
-Ecommerce tech founders
-Retailers
-Growth and marketing leaders
-Researchers studying consumer behavior and digital commerce
-Builders working on AI shopping, search, recommendation, and agent infrastructure
-Investors focused on AI and digital commerce

🎤 Who’s Taking the Stage
Ali Mirzaei - Founder & CEO of Dimension Studios

Ali Mirzaei is the founder and CEO of Dimension Studios, the social commerce company behind Seller OS, an agentic AI platform that replaces TikTok's native Seller Center with a unified operational command center for brands and agencies. Ali built the #1 shop on TikTok within six months of the platform's US launch, and Dimension has since operated four #1 shops for clients including Liquid Death, Final Boss Sour, T3 Micro, SquidHaus, Bones Coffee, and more. The company is profitable at roughly $2.5M ARR with multiple product launches planned for 2026.

Moderator: 
Alan Zong - Co-Founder & Partner at UpScaleX

Alan Zong is Co-Founder and Partner at UpScaleX, a San Francisco-based seed fund investing in AI-native applications and commercial innovations. He brings 10+ years of experience across VC and CVC and has been an early backer of multiple unicorns and decacorns. Alan holds an MBA from Harvard Business School and previously led innovation investment at Alibaba International.

💬 What We Do Not Sugarcoat
-Brand loyalty may get weaker when AI optimizes for convenience, price, and speed.
-Paid media may become less effective if discovery shifts upstream into AI interfaces.
-Consumer behavior is changing faster than most brands are planning for.
-Brands may lose access to the clickstream signals that used to reveal intent, hesitation, and purchase readiness.
-Marketplaces and retailers may lose power if agents can bypass them and go more directly to sellers or alternative paths.
-Margin pressure gets worse if AI agents consistently surface the lowest-priced option.
If your brand is invisible to AI systems, it may become invisible to future buyers.
-A direct conversation for people trying to understand what happens when commerce stops being click-first and starts becoming agent-first.

📋 What Attendees Will Walk Away With
By the end of the session, attendees should leave with a clearer understanding of:
-How agentic commerce is beginning to show up in the market already
which risks and opportunities matter most for brands and commerce platforms
-Where to invest attention now, before the shift becomes obvious to everyone
-How to think about defensibility in a world where AI increasingly mediates buyer behavior
-Who else in the room may be worth building with, learning from, or partnering with

UpScaleX - A Palo Alto–based seed fund and founders’ community investing in AI-native businesses and supporting the builders redefining how commerce is discovered, operated, and scaled.

name: NYTW Panel: VC + PE's Role in Women's Health
page_title: RSVP to NYTW Panel: VC + PE's … | Partiful
event_description:
The New Math: How VC and PE Are Rethinking Capital in Women's Health

Presented during New York Tech Week

Women's health is having a moment—but the capital backing it remains uneven. Investors are paying unprecedented attention to the category, driven by its scale, its underserved patient base, and a wave of clinical and commercial validation. Yet beneath the surface, the financing landscape is anything but straightforward. Capital remains concentrated in a small number of high-profile deals, early- and growth-stage companies face persistent cliffs, and founders often find themselves navigating a mismatch between the businesses they're building and the investment models available to them.

Meanwhile, the investors themselves are evolving. Venture capital is recalibrating its timelines, its risk tolerance, and its assumptions about what constitutes a durable women's health business. Private equity is playing an increasingly central role, building platforms and infrastructure with a fundamentally different approach to value creation and scale. These two worlds—once distinct—are beginning to converge in ways that could redefine how women's health companies are financed, operated, and brought to market. The question is no longer whether this sector matters. It's what kind of capital will shape its next chapter.

This panel brings together venture and private equity investors active in or adjacent to women's health to explore:

👉🏼 Where the capital is really going—and where it isn't

👉🏼 How investors assess opportunity across stages, sectors, and business models

👉🏼 The trade-offs between speed, scale, and sustainability in today's approaches

👉🏼 Whether hybrid VC/PE models are emerging—and how founders should prepare

👉🏼 What the current dynamics mean for the next generation of women's health companies

This is a candid, strategic conversation for investors, founders, and ecosystem builders who want a clear-eyed view of where women's health investing stands today—and where it's headed next.

🔅 Who Should Attend: Investors across venture, growth equity, and private equity; founders and operators in women's health and healthcare services; limited partners with healthcare mandates; and ecosystem builders interested in the intersection of capital strategy and care delivery.

event_description:
As robotics and automation accelerate across industries, most conversations remain abstract and focused on technology capabilities rather than real world deployment. 

Robotics adoption in U.S. manufacturing is accelerating. Nearly 400,000 industrial robots are now operating in U.S. factories, with tens of thousands added each year. At the same time, manufacturing continues to face a labor gap measured in the hundreds of thousands of open roles, with millions more projected this decade. But adoption is not the same as success. Most automation challenges do not fail at the level of technology. They fail on the factory floor, where people, process, training, safety, and operating constraints
determine whether systems work or stall.

Humans + Robots & The Factory Floor brings together operators, robotics companies, and systems leaders to explore what happens when automation meets the real world of production.

This session moves to examine the lived experience of integrating robotics into active manufacturing environments.

Why This Matters Now
Robotics adoption is increasing, but deployment challenges remain widespread. Many automation efforts fail not because of the technology itself, but because of misalignment with human systems.

Workforce, training, and operational realities are too often excluded from innovation conversations.

There is a growing need to connect startups, manufacturers, and workforce leaders in a shared dialogue.

This event addresses a critical gap by focusing on the intersection of technology an

event_description:
Who This Is For

This is not a typical hackathon.

It’s for a small group of builders who believe they can generate real alpha — but have never had access to the infrastructure to prove it.

For decades, running capital has been gated not by intelligence, but by access. Firms like Millennium Management and Citadel didn’t just hire talent — they built the machinery that turns a thesis into a managed investment operation.

That machinery is what Podium unlocks.
https://podium-finance.com/

Podium’s goal is simple:

Take the infrastructure stack of a multi-manager hedge fund and make it accessible to anyone with real edge.

We believe the next generation of strong PMs won’t come exclusively from traditional pipelines. They will come from people who already operate in complex, feedback-driven systems — but have never had the opportunity to run capital.

We’re looking for a very specific type of participant:

The founder who understands systems, feedback loops, and compounding — and sees markets as another system to model

The domain expert who knows something the market doesn’t fully price — from energy to healthcare to supply chains

The quantitative builder who can translate ideas into models, agents, or decision frameworks

The emerging PM who has the thesis, but not the $50M AUM or institutional backing

You don’t need pedigree. You don’t need a fund.

The industry over-indexes on pedigree because it has historically been the only reliable filter.

But pedigree is a proxy — not the source — of alpha.

But you do need...

1) Common sense exceeding the average 
2) Reasoning under uncertainty, and cutting through the noise
3) Extreme tenacity 

This is not for spectators. It’s for people who want to own their pipeline — from idea to execution to capital.

If you have edge, this is where you prove it.

event_description:
Artificial Intelligence is moving beyond the digital world and into the physical one. This shift, often referred to as Physical AI, is quickly becoming one of the most important frontiers in the field.

Leading AI labs, global technology companies, and a new generation of startups are building the foundations for this transition. But while progress is rapid, one question remains central: what does it actually take to make Physical AI work in practice?

NVIDIA is building the compute platforms and simulation tools. ALLSIDES is building the 3D data layer and infrastructure.

Join Franz Tschimben (CEO, ALLSIDES) and Adam Brasic (Senior Solution Architect, NVIDIA) for a fireside chat and reality check on where Physical AI stands today, what is already working, and where real value is emerging.

The conversation will explore how simulation, infrastructure, and AI come together in real-world applications, and what it takes to turn Physical AI into a viable business. It will touch on platforms such as Omniverse and Isaac Sim, the role of high-quality 3D data, and why data is increasingly becoming the bottleneck in this space.

event_description:
Fashion's been doing this for 20 years. Tech, welcome to the chat.

(Scott's take: https://worksonmymachine.ai/p/entering-technical-debts-zirp-era)

The question is whether tech learns from fashion's mistake, or repeats it at a new scale.

This Tech Week, we're hosting a happy hour of guided roundtables across tech, fashion, ops, & sustainability. 

Expert hosts leading conversations on different angles of the theme. Everyone has a chance to bring their perspective. Topics like what fast fashion does right, what tech can learn from fashion (and vice versa), infrastructure nobody sees, and what "buy it for life" means in 2026.

Expect cross-industry collaboration, a few drinks, a few laughs, and maybe some insight on how to move forward.

Tech bros, fashion girlies, investors looking for the moat, and sustainability folks who saw this coming.

Then a curated panel of creators, brand marketers, and investors will have the honest conversation about why that gap existed, who it cost the most, and what changes now that the infrastructure has caught up.

name: The convo the workplace is too polite to have
page_title: The convo the workplace is too… | Partiful
event_description:
Most high-performing women have learned to work around it. The two weeks of brain fog, mood dysregulation, fatigue, and physical symptoms that arrive every month like clockwork, and disappear just as quietly. They push through. They reschedule. They apologize for things that aren't their fault.

What they haven't been told is that this has a name, a mechanism, and a cost.

PMS and PMDD affect an estimated 3 to 8 percent of women of reproductive age at the clinical level, and up to 13 to 18 percent experience symptoms severe enough to impair function without meeting the full diagnostic threshold. The economic impact is estimated at $4,333 per woman per year in lost workplace productivity. And the last meaningful clinical innovation for this condition was the birth control pill in 1960.

This panel brings together founders, clinicians, and women with lived experience to have the conversation that workplaces, investors, and the healthcare system have been slow to have. We'll explore the emerging science, including the gut-hormone-brain axis now being studied as a key driver of premenstrual symptoms, what it means for women's performance and careers, and why this is one of the most underfunded and overlooked opportunities in women's health today.

This is not a wellness panel. It is a business, science, and human conversation about a condition that affects half the workforce.

PANELISTS:
— Roma, Founder & CEO, Pinkmatter — biotech scientist, PMDD advocate, and builder of the first gut microbiome based platform for PMS and PMDD
— Cat Duff, Podcast Host & Former Marketer — PMDD advocate bringing the lived experience and consumer perspective
— OBGYN (TBD) — practising physician and Pinkmatter practitioner partner, bringing the clinical lens on how PMS and PMDD are (and aren't) being addressed in practice
— TBD — founder in tech

FORMAT: Panel discussion followed by Q&A and networking reception
DURATION: 90 minutes
ATTENDANCE: ~50
AUDIENCE: Femtech founders, investors, operators, women's health professionals, press, and high-performing women navigating these conditions personally

---

WHY THIS EVENT FOR TECH WEEK:
The economic cost of untreated PMS and PMDD is measurable, significant, and almost entirely absent from the workplace conversation. As women's health becomes one of the fastest-growing investment categories in tech, this panel puts the science, the founder building solutions, and the clinical expertise in the same room as the investors and operators who can accelerate change. The performance tax framing makes this a business conversation as much as a health one, and that's exactly what Tech Week audiences are here for.

event_description:
Loop is an invite-only supper on the recursive patterns behind the physical economy — control loops, feedback loops, scaling laws.

It's for founders and investors working in manufacturing, field services, construction, energy, logistics, defense, and humanoids — the companies where revenue is earned at an address, not a URL.

Most tech dinners happen in the world of bits — SaaS metrics, model benchmarks, ARR curves. Loop is the other table. It's for the people building and backing the companies where revenue is earned at a job site, a factory floor, a warehouse, or an address on a map.

The conversation has one spine: the recursive patterns that govern physical revenue. Control loops. Feedback loops. Scaling laws. The physical world doesn't compound like software — but it does compound. Understanding how is the whole game.

Twelve seats, one long table, a pop-up chef, and natural wine from growers around the globe. Five courses built on a single scaling rule. An Escher print on the menu, a Duchamp quote chosen for each guest, and a quiet personalization on each plate. No decks, no panels, no pitches.

Loop is hosted by Allometry — the Agentic OS for physical revenue. Modern industrial operators run every commercial decision through Allometry: every quote, every contract, every dispatch, scored against margin and EV at the address level. The same control layer that underwrites a quote today makes labor, machines, and humanoids programmable tomorrow.

The dinner isn't about Allometry. It's about the people at the table.

Greenpoint. $295/seat + service. Covers chef, wine pairing, and room. Waived for Allometry design partners. Every seat earns 1 Loop — a free underwriting review on a real job, redeemable whenever, or giftable to a portfolio company.

event_description:
💡 What’s the Ugly Truth

Beauty tech is booming, but growth has made the category louder, not clearer. AI diagnostics, AR try-ons, personalization, and smart devices are pulling more founders into the space, but more innovation also means more hype, more copycats, and more brands fighting for the same customer attention.

For founders, a strong product is just the entry fee. The real edge comes from knowing what actually drives trust, repeat purchase, and loyalty in a market where branding and novelty can fake momentum. This room is for people who want to separate signal from noise and figure out which trends are truly shaping the future of beauty tech.

🎯 Why You Should Attend

- Hear from a pioneer in beauty tech and understand what they are building, how they got there, and what they are paying attention to now.
- Connect with other beauty tech founders who are relentlessly innovating and building through the noise.
- Understand shifting consumer behavior, changing demand, and what customers are looking for now.

- Beauty tech founders
- Beauty business owners
- Consumer and brand experts
- Investors interested in beauty tech and consumer companies

Zehra Soysal - Founder & CEO of Savanah.ai

Zehra's career journey began at Google in business strategy, followed by impactful roles at BCG, where she worked across diverse sectors in Europe, the Middle East, and Asia. She played a key role in establishing a tech joint venture with Turkey's largest conglomerate, igniting her passion for innovative business technologies. She earned her MBA from Harvard Business School in 2022. Post-MBA, she joined Metaphysic.ai in New York, where she was instrumental in scaling operations and driving strategic growth through its $1.4B acquisition. She is now the founder and CEO of Savanah.ai, a New York-based visual AI platform helping brands create e-commerce imagery at scale and optimize conversion.

More speakers coming soon!

💬 What We Do Not Sugarcoat

- In an industry full of noise and competition, how do you separate real signal from hype?
- How do you fight copycats in a market where products move fast and differentiation can disappear overnight?
- What trends actually reflect customer demand, and what are customers burning for now that they were not asking for before?
- How does AI actually matter here, from diagnostics and personalization to discovery, conversion, and retention?

name: AI x Longevity Summit
all_hosts: Longevity Global; Dovetail Biopartners; Yale University
page_title: AI x Longevity Summit - #NYTec… | Partiful
event_description:
NOTE: You MUST buy a ticket through Eventbrite to attend. Your registration on Partiful does not give you event access.

Purchase your ticket here: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/ai-x-longevity-nyc-tickets-1987706522717

June 4–5, 2026 | BioLabs@NYU Langone, Long Island City, Queens

Longevity science is at an inflection point. Foundation models are learning the language of biology, aging clocks are quantifying human health with new precision, and a generation of therapeutics and clinical platforms is emerging to act on those signals.

The inaugural theme of the Summit, Signal to Intervention, explores how AI is compressing the distance between discovery and real-world impact.

As a flagship event of Longevity Global NYC, the AI x Longevity Summit convenes the researchers, clinicians, founders, and engineers building the next generation of longevity infrastructure. Hosted at BioLabs@NYU Langone in the heart of the city's biotech corridor, the Summit is where technical depth meets translational ambition.

Find this year's agenda, speaker lineup, and pitch competition information here: https://longevitygl.org/nyc-ai-x-longevity-summit/

What We'll Cover

Day 1: Signal — From Models to Biology

Day 1 grounds AI in the realities of biological systems and examines what current capabilities mean for discovery and company building.

Foundation models in drug discovery, target identification, and biomarker development
Aging clocks and the science of measuring human health at new resolution
The role of data quality, experimental design, and infrastructure in producing meaningful AI outputs
Where models are delivering real signal versus where they remain limited
Platform strategy, data acquisition, and differentiation for AI-native bio companies
The investment landscape across AI x Bio and how capital is being deployed

Day 2: Intervention — From Models to Patients

Day 2 shifts to deployment: how AI is being put to work in clinics, care models, and regulated environments, and what it takes to scale.

AI in longevity clinics and preventative care
Continuous monitoring, digital health, and real-world data integration
Clinical decision support and personalized intervention strategies
Regulatory and policy considerations at the intersection of AI and healthcare

What it takes to move from model to deployment across real patient populations

Day 2 also features the live pitch competition finals for Seed and Series A companies building at the intersection of AI and longevity. Winners receive lab bench and desk space at BioLabs @ NYU Langone, and finalists pitch directly to investors, clinicians, and pharma BD teams in the room.

Who This Is For

The Summit is designed for people actively building and deploying at this intersection:

Scientists applying AI to aging biology and disease
Founders building AI-driven therapeutics, platforms, and diagnostics
Investors focused on AI x Bio and digital health
Clinicians and operators integrating AI into care models
Pharma and BD teams evaluating new technologies
Engineers and data scientists working on real biological and clinical systems

The format is intentionally curated to prioritize substantive exchange over scale, the kind of room where conversations go deeper and the connections actually move work forward.

name: How Growth-Stage Companies Are Scaling Marketing
page_title: How Growth-Stage Companies Are… | Partiful
event_description:
ABOUT THE WEBINAR

Growth-stage companies face the same problem over and over. The board approves an aggressive pipeline target. The headcount budget does not move. The CMO is expected to close that gap with the same team, the same spend, and a stack of tools that were supposed to make everything easier, but mostly created more coordination work.

The reflex most marketing companies reach for is another tool. Another platform. Another dashboard. And six months later, the team is managing tooling instead of driving growth, output has not materially improved, and the gap between what leadership expects and what marketing delivers has quietly gotten wider.

The companies that are actually closing that gap right now are not doing it by adding people or buying more software. They are doing it by building infrastructure: AI-powered marketing systems where research, campaign execution, paid media optimization, lead nurturing, and performance reporting operate as a connected sequence rather than as disconnected tasks scattered across a team that is already stretched.

That is what this session is about.

On June 4, as part of Tech Week New York 2026, Hamlet Azarian, Founder and CEO of Azarian Growth Agency, will demonstrate exactly how those systems work: live, starting from a blank screen. Not a recorded demo. Not a slide deck with hypothetical outputs. 

A working system, built and run in real time, across the functions that matter most to a growth-stage marketing operation: demand generation, paid media, pipeline development, and performance analytics.

Azarian Growth Agency works directly with CMOs and marketing leaders at growth-stage companies, navigating precisely this pressure: boards demanding 2x results with flat resources, marketing teams that are capable but over-extended, and AI tools that have produced volume without strategic direction. 

The systems we will demonstrate in this session are the same ones built and operated for those companies. You will leave this session with a clear picture of what AI marketing systems can realistically handle across the full funnel, where human strategic judgment remains non-negotiable, and how to evaluate whether your team should build, buy, or partner to get there. 

You will also leave with a practical diagnostic framework you can run against your own marketing operation the same week, not a theoretical exercise, but a structured way to identify where operational drag is costing you the most and where AI systems would create the fastest lift.

This session is designed for CMOs and VPs of Marketing who are past the AI curiosity phase. If you have already tried the tools and found that they produce activity without outcomes, this is the session that shows you why, and what the alternative looks like in practice.

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

Everything in this session is built around one question: how does a growth-stage marketing team do more, with the team it already has?

1. Why your current AI tool stack is making your team less productive, not more 

The problem is not the tools. The problem is that tools without a system layer create fragmentation: more inputs, more handoffs, more editing cycles, and more time spent managing software instead of driving growth. The webinar will show exactly where that breakdown happens and what the structural fix looks like across a real marketing operation.

2. What an AI-powered marketing system actually is, and how it differs from what most teams have built 

There is a meaningful difference between a collection of AI tools and a marketing system. A system connects strategy, execution, optimization, and reporting in sequence, so output moves without constant manual intervention. We show you what that architecture looks like across demand generation, paid media, pipeline nurturing, and analytics, and where each function fits.

3. A live demonstration: an AI marketing system built and run in real time 

No prerecorded demo. No best-case scenario constructed in advance. We will build and run a working AI marketing system live during the session, showing exactly which components connect, how decisions get made at each stage, what the output looks like across channels, and where human oversight is required. If something does not run cleanly in the moment, you will see that too.

4. How to scale paid media performance without scaling the team managing it 

Paid media is one of the highest-leverage places to apply AI infrastructure, and one of the most commonly mismanaged. The session will cover how AI systems handle campaign monitoring, bid strategy signals, audience segmentation updates, and performance reporting in a way that reduces the manual workload on your team without removing the strategic judgment that actually moves ROAS and CAC.

5. Pipeline development and lead nurturing at scale without proportional headcount

Building and maintaining a pipeline is operationally expensive. We will show you how AI systems handle lead scoring, nurture sequence logic, timing optimization, and handoff signals to sales so your team is focused on high-value conversations instead of the mechanics of keeping the pipeline moving.

6. How to connect your marketing system to the metrics your board actually cares about

The board is not asking about impressions or publish frequency. They are asking about CAC, LTV, pipeline contribution, and payback period. You will learn how AI marketing systems get built around revenue metrics from the start, not retrofitted after the fact, and what that connection looks like in a reporting layer your leadership team can actually read.

7. Where human strategic judgment is non-negotiable in an AI marketing system 

The marketing organizations that fail with AI do so because they automate the wrong layer. Positioning, ICP targeting, messaging hierarchy, and offer strategy are not tasks for a system to own. We will show you where humans must remain in the loop and how to structure a system that handles execution without losing the strategic coherence that makes execution matter.

8. How growth-stage companies are running more campaigns with smaller teams 

Real examples from companies operating in the same conditions your team is in right now: flat headcount, growing pipeline targets, boards that want board-ready attribution. We walk through what the setup looked like, what changed operationally when the system went live, and what the output difference was across paid, organic, and lifecycle channels.

MEET THE SPEAKER

Hamlet Azarian has spent 20+ years doing one thing: figuring out why growth-stage companies plateau, and building the systems that move them forward. He founded Azarian Growth Agency as a full-funnel, data-driven growth firm, and has since helped companies across SaaS, e-commerce, fintech, and B2B tech raise over $300M and build marketing engines that scale without proportional headcount growth.

He is not a theorist. The AI marketing systems he will demonstrate in this session are the same ones his team builds and runs for clients. His work sits at the intersection of performance marketing, AI-native workflow design, and revenue operations, and his standard for a useful session is simple: you should be able to use what you learn the same week you learn it.

Hamlet also works directly with portfolio company marketing and leadership teams, which gives him a specific vantage point on what growth-stage CMOs are actually facing at the board level right now.
He has led 17 previous sessions in [A] Growth Lab webinar series, covering advanced Google Ads, Meta strategy, email infrastructure, server-side tracking, GEO, vibe marketing, and generative AI, consistently drawing senior marketing leaders who want operational depth, not surface-level overviews.

name: Your Next Exec Won't Be Human
all_hosts: Masinov Company / Claw Mart; Build Momentum
page_title: RSVP to Your Next Exec Won't B… | Partiful
event_description:
The startup org chart is breaking.

Founders are under pressure to move faster, stay leaner, and build more with less. But the old answer (hire a full executive team, add more headcount, and hope the org chart catches up) no longer works for most early-stage companies.

At the same time, two new forms of leverage are changing how startups operate: AI agents and senior fractional.

AI agents open up a nearly infinite set of opportunities to automate tasks, redesign workflows, monitor execution, and support day-to-day operations.

Fractional leaders give founders access to experienced operators across go-to-market, product, operations, finance, engineering, design, people, and strategy without the cost or commitment of premature full-time hires. 

But for early-stage founders, the hard part is knowing how to put those pieces together.

Which roles need senior human judgment? Which functions should be fractional before they become full-time? Which tasks are ready for agents? What should stay founder-led, what should be delegated to expert operators, and what should become an AI-enabled workflow?

This NY Tech Week session helps founders answer those questions.

Felix, the AI CEO of The Masinov Company, Build Momentum, and Founders & Fractionals will guide founders through a practical, hands-on session for redesigning the early-stage operating team around founder ownership, fractional talent, future full-time hires, and AI agents.

The program includes:

A quick demystification of AI agents for early-stage founders
What agents are, what they can realistically do today, where they are useful, and where the hype gets ahead of reality.

A focused discussion on building with fractional talent
How founders can access senior operators across key functions without overhiring too early, and how to scope fractional support around outcomes instead of vague advisory work.

An interactive operating team mapping exercise
Participants will identify the tasks, roles, workflows, and bottlenecks inside their business, then draft the ideal mix of founder ownership, fractional leaders, full-time hires, and AI agents.

A real-world AI executive example
Felix will show how an AI executive can support prioritization, execution, monitoring, follow-up, and day-to-day company management inside a real operating business.

Founders will leave with a first draft of their hybrid operating roadmap: what to own, what to fractionalize, what to hire for later, and what to turn into AI-agent workflows.

50–70% of private equity deals fail to create value. The reason is almost never financial. 

It's Stakeholder Risk .

From regulators and employees to local communities and strategic partners, mismanaging stakeholder dynamics can erode value just as quickly as strong alignment can accelerate it. 

As AI rapidly reshapes industries, a new layer of risk is emerging making stakeholder alignment more critical than ever. 

This session explores how leading firms identify, quantify, and proactively manage stakeholder risk, including AI-related exposures, as a core lever of value creation.

Featuring: 

Jennifer G. Bates, founder & CEO of HumanFactor Enterprises, a stakeholder risk Intelligence platform.
 
Known for her ability to see what others cannot, Jennifer Baytes transforms Stakeholder Risk and decision-making into structured, data-driven frameworks. Her work has contributed to outcomes including valuation increases of up to 800%, $140M+ in M&A readiness and transaction positioning, multi-million-dollar exits, and over $600M in enterprise value creation.

Key discussion points:

Why stakeholder risk is often overlooked in traditional PE due diligence

How misalignment with regulators, employees, or communities can destroy deal value

The rise of AI-related stakeholder risks: bias, transparency, data privacy, and regulatory backlash

Frameworks for identifying and mapping key stakeholders across the investment lifecycle

Real-world case studies: where stakeholder dynamics drove unexpected outcomes

Integrating stakeholder and AI risk into value creation plans and exit strategies

Preparing portfolio companies for AI governance

event_description:
On the Digital Health Inside Out YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@DigitalHealthInsideOut), there are monthly series called Digital Health Vitals — where experts talk through the latest digital health news, grade recent fundraises and public company earnings, and share an honest take on what’s working and what’s not.
For this event, we’re bringing that same format to Health2Tech — live.
We’ll be recording an episode on stage with the lineup of experts, reacting to breaking news, debating a bit, playing a couple of games, and opening it up for Q&A with the audience.
If you want to hear real perspectives and get a feel for what’s happening in healthtech right now, this is the must-attend event. 

​🕕 Event Schedule:

​5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome and a chance to settle in.

​6:00 - 6:45 Digital Health Vitals, Live Recording!

6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, and collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.

🤩 About our Guest Speaker:

​​Host/Moderator: ​​ 

Alex Koshykov (https://www.linkedin.com/in/alex-koshykov/) is a co-founder of BeKey (https://bekey.io/) and a digital health expert who constantly shares news, introduces promising technologies, and promotes secure software & hardware for the healthcare industry on his YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/c/BeKey-Hub). Additionally, he is a co-founder of YODD (https://igg.me/at/yodd), a medical device startup. 

Experts: 

Sergei Polevikov (https://www.linkedin.com/in/sergeiai/) has decades of deep experience in math, statistics, and AI, with four graduate degrees spanning mathematics, economics, finance, and machine learning. He has authored over 30 peer-reviewed publications and manuscripts. His work is driven by a relentless pursuit of brutal truth in healthcare. That mission has led him to become not just a founder of successful healthcare AI and digital health startups, but also a healthcare fraud investigator. Today, Sergei is focused on health AI education and truth-telling. He runs the podcast “Digital Health Inside Out” (https://www.youtube.com/@DigitalHealthInsideOut) (with his co-host Alex Koshykov) and the Substack “AI Health Uncut“ (http://sergeiai.substack.com/), which has grown rapidly to over 8,000 subscribers in just a few short months. 

Stephanie Davis (https://www.linkedin.com/in/stephjdavis/) is a Managing Director and senior research analyst covering Healthcare Technology and Distribution. She joined Barclays in 2023 following over a decade of experience covering the Healthcare Technology and IT Services sectors. Prior to joining Barclays, Ms. Davis led coverage of the Healthcare Technology sector at SVB Securities, Citibank, and J.P. Morgan. Prior to Healthcare Technology, Ms. Davis was an Equity Research Analyst at J.P. Morgan on the #1 ranked Payments, Processors, and IT Services team. Ms. Davis ranked #3 in the Institutional Investor 2023 All America Research Team for Healthcare Technology and Distribution, and was recognized as a Runner-Up in both 2019 and 2022. She was included in Business Insider’s “Rising Stars of Equity Research” in 2017. Ms. Davis earned a B.A. in Economics and Mathematics from Columbia University and is a CFA charterholder. She is a member of the Board of Trustees for The New York Foundling.

​Guy Milhalter (https://www.linkedin.com/in/guymilhalter/) is a business-minded technology transactions attorney who advises technology companies, startups, and health IT companies on complex, strategic transactions. He regularly counsels clients on legal risk, governance, and the commercial deployment of AI technologies. ​Guy frequently supports legal and business teams in fast-paced environments where deal execution, regulatory compliance, and business strategy intersect.

🌟 Why Attend?

​Meet like-minded individuals who are actively shaping the health tech landscape.

​Share experiences, discuss challenges, and explore potential solutions with fellow founders.

​Learn from the journeys of other entrepreneurs, discover something new, seek advice, and perhaps find the mentor or partner you've been looking for.

​🤝 Who Should Attend?

​Digital Health Founders at various stages of their startup journey.

​Healthcare Professionals who are passionate about health innovation.

​Investors looking to make impactful contributions to the digital health and medtech spaces.

​🚀 Why This Event Is A Must?

​Hear from thought leaders and innovators in the digital health domain (at every event, we'll have a new set of speakers).

​Connect with peers, potential collaborators, and mentors.

​Participate in engaging Q&As and discussions that can spark new ideas and opportunities.

​🏙️ Venue Details:

​Great location in the heart of New York, equipped to foster conversations and connections. Venue details will be shared with registered attendees. Because of limited capacity, we won't be able to accommodate everyone, so please register whenever you are sure you can attend.

​Don’t miss this chance to be part of a community that’s driving the future of health tech. Reserve your spot now and join us in shaping the landscape of digital health for 2026 and beyond.

Partners

​​Pearl Cohen (https://www.pearlcohen.com) is an international law firm with offices in New York, Boston, San Francisco, Tel Aviv, London, and Munich. Representing innovation-driven companies, inventors, and their investors, we serve clients worldwide, from Fortune 500 companies to leading academic institutions and promising start-ups. With professionals coming from a wide variety of academic and professional backgrounds, our team is your partner in the business of innovation.

J.P. Morgan (https://www.jpmorgan.com/commercial-banking/startups) serves venture-backed and high-growth startups, founders, and venture capital firms across the globe. We provide deep industry expertise, local support, global products and services, and a robust network of investors and partners to meet your commercial, investment, and private banking needs. 

​​Additionally, J.P. Morgan has a complimentary Cap Table solution that is complimentary for up to 40 stakeholders. If you’ve been looking for an alternative way to manage your firm’s equity ownership and bring your reward strategy to life, please reach out.

About the organizer

​Alex Koshykov is a co-founder of BeKey and a digital health expert who constantly shares news, introduces promising technologies, and promotes secure software & hardware for the healthcare industry on his YouTube channel. Additionally to that, he is a co-founder of YODD, a medical device startup.

Bailey Morgan, Based in Astoria, NYC, is a versatile healthtech leader who merges clinical expertise with business acumen to accelerate healthcare innovation and community impact. Having started her career as a medical speech language pathologist working within inpatient facilities throughout the boroughs of NYC, she saw firsthand how behind the healthcare tech ecosystem was compared to industries such as tech or finance.

After leaving healthcare to move into the healthtech startup space, Bailey has since raised over $10M in capital, led several successful sales and marketing teams through go-to-market stages in both SaaS and CPG, and has closed over $2M in technology sales herself. She currently serves as Chief of Staff at Groth Pain & Spine, a pain management practice with 10+ locations and 40+ providers, where she leads the change management and technology integrations for the practices acquisitions.

In addition to consulting with various healthcare technology companies, Bailey is a Director and the Treasurer for an NYC-based dementia-focused nonprofit that employs individuals living with dementia and supports families and caregivers.

Additional Information

By signing up, your email will be automatically added to the Health2Tech newsletter with news and upcoming events — but don’t worry, we won’t flood your inbox! ;) 

Also, just a note that this event might be photographed or filmed. If we do capture some moments, Health2Tech may use the photos or videos for marketing and communication purposes. By registering, you're giving us the thumbs up for using your image for these reasons.

name: Executive Data Council: Evening Roundtables
Vertical AI in Accounting with CPA.com, Adaptive, and Tabs
page_title: RSVP to Vertical AI in Account… | Partiful
event_description:
Join us for an evening of drinks, networking, and a conversation the accounting profession is overdue for.

General-purpose AI is impressive. It can summarize, draft, and reason across an enormous range of tasks. But accounting and tax aren't general problems. They're governed by rules that change, edge cases that carry liability, and judgment calls that no model gets right just by being large. That gap, between what AI can do and what accounting actually demands, is where the most consequential work in the profession is happening right now.

This panel brings together thought leaders, firm leaders from the profession, and the builders working at that frontier to share what's working in practice, where the hype still outpaces reality, and what separates AI that holds up in an accounting environment from AI that doesn't.

If you're leading a firm or advising one, this is a conversation worth being in the room for.

Joining us for the panel:

Seema Amble, Partner at a16z (moderator)
Richard Kopelman, CEO of Aprio
Erik Asgeirsson, President & CEO of CPA.com
Matt Calvano, CEO & Co-Founder of Adaptive

event_description:
⚡ IRL or Nothing: A Meetup for People Building Human Connection in the Age of AI

NYC Tech Week · Founders · Investors · Builders

We’re in a strange moment. AI is everywhere. Screens are smarter. And somehow — people have never felt more alone.

If you’re building apps that get people off their phones and into the same room, that use technology as a bridge not a barrier, that believe proximity, serendipity, and real human chemistry still matter — this is your people.

We’re bringing together IRL social founders, investors, and innovators for an evening of honest conversation, big ideas, and the kind of connections you can’t make in a DM.

Expect a panel, expect good chat, expect to meet someone who’s grappling with the exact same thing you are.

We’ll get into:

• What’s actually broken about social media — and what IRL apps can fix

• Building for human connection in a world that keeps optimising for engagement

• The investor lens: where does this space go from here?

name: Stop Making AI Guess: When Your Codebase Becomes the Spec
page_title: RSVP to Stop Making AI Guess: … | Partiful
event_description:
If AI should read codebase structure rather than guess at it, why doesn't it?

AI coding tools work by reading source files and inferring architecture. The result is "almost-usable" code that requires manual refactoring. 

The deeper problem isn't the tools — it's that most frameworks weren't designed to be read structurally. There's no layer for AI to reason against, so the tools are stuck guessing.

SpyneJS is an open-source framework designed for AI-assisted development. It exposes a structural codemap that gives agents a deterministic understanding of application structure.

Refined over six years in enterprise environments, the framework is designed so generated code respects architectural boundaries from the first prompt.

Join us for a live demo of frontend codegen that holds up under peer review. We'll show how agents interact with SpyneJS to produce structurally sound features, then discuss what becomes possible when the codebase itself functions as a working specification.

For developers, founders, and anyone evaluating where serious frontend development goes next.

spynejs.com

name: AI-Native Services: Why SaaS is Dead
page_title: RSVP to AI-Native Services: Wh… | Partiful
event_description:
Services markets — legal, finance, insurance, compliance — represent over $1 trillion globally. For decades, software made those service providers faster, but the margin stayed with the firms. AI is collapsing that distinction. Companies are no longer selling tools to service providers; they are owning both the intelligence layer and the delivery itself.

This panel brings together a curated group of founders building in that category, alongside the investors backing them, to work through the questions that are top of mind in the space right now: Where does AI replace the service, and where does it only make the service faster?
